name: devharness

tools.name: connection
tools.description: Debugger connections to Chrome or Node.js; every other tool names one by `connection`.

newName.description: rename: the new name, 3 descriptive words

reason.description: close: why the connection is closed

url.description: launch: URL to open (default: blank page)

port.description: launch: debugging port (default: this session's reserved port); a Chrome already on it gets a tab. attach: debugger port (Node.js usually 9229)

autoConnect.description: launch: connect the debugger after launch (default: true)

forceNewInstance.description: launch: a fresh Chrome process, never a tab in an existing one

newContextWindow.description: launch: a window in the Chrome on `port` with cookies and storage of its own; with proxy, only it routes through the proxy

copyCookiesFrom.description: launch with newContextWindow: the connection whose cookies the new window starts with

bringToFront.description: launch/switch: select this tab and raise Chrome, taking keyboard focus (default: false)

width.description: launch: viewport width in CSS px

height.description: launch: viewport height in CSS px

profile.description: launch: named persistent Chrome profile, e.g. "device-a", whose storage survives across runs

proxy.description: launch: route this browser through an intercepting proxy, so a response or socket frame can be held and served in its place (default: false)

chromeArgs.description: launch: extra Chrome command-line flags, merged after the managed defaults

watchInput.description: launch: record a person's clicks and typing in this browser into History and onto the next reply, as the bench's RECORD MY INPUT does (default: replay.watchPersonInput)

tools.name: browser
tools.description: The Chrome processes this session launched; apart from connection so allowing connection allows no kill.

reason.description: Why the browser is killed or the launcher reset

port.description: kill: the Chrome to kill (default: every Chrome this session launched)

tools.name: breakpoint
tools.description: Breakpoints and logpoints.

tools.name: execution

connection.description: The connection, by the name connection launch or attach gave it; acknowledge without one covers every paused connection

isRegex.description: searchCode: pattern is a regex (default: true)

directory.description: loadMaps: the directory whose .js.map files, subdirectories included, are registered

connection.description: get: the connection, by the name connection launch or attach gave it

tools.name: console
tools.description: Console messages, from the page or a worker via `target`.

type.description: Message type filter (log, error, warn, etc.)

argsIndex.description: Specific args array index to return

reason.description: Why console needs clearing (required for clear)

tools.name: network
tools.description: Network traffic as CDP sees it; proxy holds what reached the outside world.

connection.description: The connection, by the name connection launch or attach gave it

tools.description: Read and steer the intercepting proxy a browser was launched through (launch with proxy: true); holding traffic in time is the hold tool.

direction.description: answerFrame: only messages going this way

tools.name: hold
tools.description: Stop the app across its layers and step it. Layers: code (JS paused), ui (page time, CSS, media, input; JS runs; needs the bench), network (proxy).

tools.name: navigate
tools.description: Navigate the page; goto, reload, back and forward return its console and failed-request counts and cache its interactive elements for 5 min. info: URL, title, viewport. viewport: sets the page's viewport by emulation, leaving the window as it is; a run puts back the viewport it began with when it ends.

connection.description: The connection, by the name connection launch or attach gave it

url.description: URL to navigate to (required for goto action)

waitUntil.description: goto/reload: when navigation counts as complete (default load)

width.description: viewport: CSS px wide; with height. Both omitted, the page follows its window again

height.description: viewport: CSS px tall; with width

tools.name: dom
tools.description: Inspect and query the DOM.

connection.description: The connection, by the name connection launch or attach gave it

tools.name: screenshot
tools.description: Visual verification only; extractText reads content.

tileWidth.description: burst: widest tile on the sheet (default 320)

tools.name: input
tools.description: Browser input; hold, holdBeforeFrame and burst take the hold or the frames in the same call.

expect.description: click/type/hover: the element meant, as a fingerprint; another element is not acted on

append.description: Append text instead of replacing (default: false)

insert.description: type: put the text in as one trusted input event (CDP Input.insertText), as a paste or an IME commit does, in place of a keystroke per character; keydown and keyup handlers do not see it

gapsMs.description: press with keys: ms from each key to the next

direction.description: swipe: direction across `selector`'s box, read at run time; in a list it holds where from/to drift with the rows above

burst.description: Record the frames the compositor swaps from the dispatch on, saved under .devharness/screenshots with a contact sheet; with hold, the capture ends at the hold

tools.name: content
tools.description: Primary tool for page content; prefer over screenshots.

connection.description: The connection, by the name connection launch or attach gave it

mode.description: extractText: outline (headings and metadata), full (entire page), section (one section by heading)

checks.description: verify: handlers (dead buttons), viewport (position), touch (target size), overflow (clipping), clickability (z-index blocking, slow), links (dead hrefs), scroll (horizontal). Default: all but clickability

waitMs.description: parse: max ms to wait for the plugin's waitFor predicate (default 8000; 0 skips)

tools.name: modal
tools.description: Browser dialogs and page overlays.

tools.description: Open the bench beside a driven app: hold the page still, read what crossed its boundary and what caused each thing, record and step sequences, and collect element-level comments.

instructions:
# devharness MCP Server

Chrome DevTools Protocol debugging for JavaScript/TypeScript in Chrome, Node.js, or CDP-compatible environments - breakpoints, variable inspection, browser automation, dev server management, and record/replay verification.

**Quick start (web apps):**
1. `connection({ action: 'launch', connection: "my-web-app" })` - launches AND auto-connects, ready immediately (do not attach after this)
2. `navigate({ action: 'goto', connection: "my-web-app", url: "..." })` - also caches interactive elements for the page
3. `content({ action: 'findInteractive', connection: "my-web-app" })` / `content({ action: 'extractText', mode: 'outline', connection: "my-web-app" })` to read the page
4. Use other tools with `connection: "my-web-app"`

**Node.js:** start with `node --inspect=9229 app.js`, then `connection({ action: 'attach', connection: "my-web-app", port: 9229 })`.

Each tool's description, and the reply of its first use in a session, carry how to use it. The full reference is `docs/instructions.md` in the devharness package.

If devharness itself seems stuck or broken (not the target app), restart it yourself: `config({ action: 'restart' })` (falls back to `kill -USR2 $(cat .devharness/mcp-supervisor.pid)` if that's unavailable). This kills any Chrome instances it launched (relaunch with `connection` action `launch`); managed dev servers (`server` tool) survive this restart and reattach. Ending the session or `/reload-plugins` stops the servers this session started.
